That premise is false, and a reading shows it: the committee's own site carries a page dedicated to this one subcommittee, linked from https://naturalresources.house.gov/ as "Energy and Mineral Resources" and reached at this URL. Probed 2026-09-18 with scripts/probe_candidate_pages.py: 4,439 readable characters (well above the verifier's 400-character floor) and the verifier's own label test matches in the CONTENT region as "Energy and Mineral Resources | House Committee on Natural Resources", rule=committee_scaffolding_folded — the fold this project already grants a node of type Subcommittee, with more than two tokens left in the core. The subcommittee is current, not a stale name: the House Clerk's committed list (tests/fixtures/directories/house/committees.xlsx) files "Energy and Mineral Resources" (II06) under II00. WHAT PROMOTING THIS COSTS, stated so it can be declined: the node is confirmed today through inheritance from https://naturalresources.house.gov/, where it matched by exact equality as "Subcommittee on <name>"; candidate_urls stops at distance 0, so once the node has an entry of its own it stops inheriting, and this page matches only by the committee fold (no fragment on it equals the full curated name, which is why the probe reports a folded rule rather than equality). What is gained is not just the stronger method string: today this node's existence and its placement rest on one fetch of one page counted twice, and after promotion existence comes from the subcommittee's own page while the listed placement block still rests on the committee's homepage — two observations of two pages instead of one. The risk is the ordinary own-page risk plus a query-string CMS path that could rot; the verifier re-fetches and re-decides, and if it ever 404s this node falls back to nothing rather than to the parent page.
